title: A nice workflow for generating basic 3d assets I am using
author: HuWeiliu
selftext:
I've been struggling with the need to express all my wishes in words, especially for changing cosmetic stuff.

I got Claude to setup a skill and a website served locally (on my PC) that will support receiving images. The website can also display those images, and lets me draw on top of them.

On my iPad, I go into procreate, draw the asset I want. I copy it and use a shortcut to send it to the local server. This can include handwritten prompts on it. 

Claude picks up the image on my PC and builds a model through blender of my drawing. It then presents a render of that model as an image, which I can open on the website on my ipad, and make modifications through drawing on it. It gets sent back to Claude, who takes in the modifications and builds it again.

This way I can set the art direction through my own art. I can express my desires through images rather than words, and the process is fast and seamless.

The game picks up the models by name, so I can easily change any model in game by simply drawing over it on my iPad.

comments.author: Mamaun30
comments.body: Great workflow. Can you show some images of the process?

comments.author: Illustrious-Pay6341
comments.body: Eyy! I use something similar. Claude created me artifact page where I can upload a sketch and then there is a loop running in my claude code that waits for the queued item, picks up the job, uses blender mcp to create the 3d model, takes pictures of the model, uploads them to artifact webpage and marks the item to be reviewed. Then I can look at the image or go to blender directly and look at the model, suggest changes and put the item back in queue or mark them as complete. :)

comments.author: Disastrous-Gain5870
comments.body: This is really cool. I’d love to see some images. I think stuff like this is the future of art in games. It allows us to keep OUR taste while speeding up the process with AI immensely.
